NONE: › to send air out of your lungs
呼出，吐出（肺中的空氣），呼氣

example: Take a deep breath in then exhale into the mouthpiece.
深呼吸，然後將氣吹入樂器吹口中。

T: C1 to make someone extremely tired
使筋疲力竭；使疲憊不堪

NONE: C1 the waste gas from an engine, especially a car's, or the pipe the gas flows through
（引擎排出的）廢氣；（尤指汽車的）尾氣；排氣管

example: The long journey exhausted the children.
長途旅行後，孩子們疲憊不堪。
I've exhausted myself with all that cleaning.
打掃累得我筋疲力盡。
How long will it be before the world's fuel supplies are exhausted?
再過多長時間地球上的燃料就耗盡了？
I'm afraid he's exhausted my patience.
恐怕我對他已經失去耐性了。
We seem to have exhausted this topic of conversation (= we have nothing new to say about it).
這個話題我們好像已經沒有甚麼好談的了。
Car exhaust is the main reason for the city's pollution.
汽車排出的廢氣是造成城市污染的主要原因。

NONE: › a piece of equipment used to remove steam, smoke, or unpleasant smells from a room or building
排氣風扇
› the pipe at the back of a vehicle or on a machine through which waste gas escapes from the engine
（車輛）排氣管
B1 extremely tired
極其疲憊的；精疲力竭的

example: Exhausted, they fell asleep.
他們筋疲力盡，倒頭就睡。
By the time they reached the summit they were exhausted.
他們上到山頂時，已經筋疲力竭了。

NONE: › Exhaustible supplies of something can be used completely so there are none left.
可耗盡的；會枯竭的

example: It is clear that many of the earth's resources are exhaustible.
顯然，地球上很多資源都不是取之不盡用之不竭的。

NONE: B2 making you feel extremely tired
使人筋疲力竭的；使人疲憊不堪的

example: I've had an exhausting day.
忙完一天使我筋疲力竭。

NONE: B2 the state of being extremely tired
筋疲力竭；疲憊不堪

example: She felt ill with/from exhaustion.
她過度勞累，終於病了。

NONE: C1 complete and including everything
徹底的；詳盡的；全面的

example: an exhaustive study/report
全面的研究／詳盡的報告

NONE: C1 to show something publicly
展出，展覽；展示
C1 an object that is shown to the public in a museum, etc.
展品；展出物；陳列品
C1 US UK exhibition a collection of objects that is shown to the public in a museum, etc.
（一批）展品，展覽
› specialized law a thing used as evidence (= proof that something is true) in a trial
（法庭上出示的）證據，物證

example: He frequently exhibits at the art gallery.
他經常在藝廊展出作品。
In the summer the academy will exhibit several prints that are rarely seen.
該學會將於今年夏天對外展出幾幅罕見的版畫作品。
He exhibited great self-control considering her rudeness.
她那麼無禮，他表現得如此克制已經很好了。
The museum has a fascinating collection of exhibits ranging from Iron Age pottery to Inuit clothing.
這個博物館收藏的展品，從鐵器時代的陶器，到因努伊特人的衣物，豐富多彩，令人稱奇。
Let's go see the new dinosaur exhibit.
我們去看這個有關恐龍的新展覽吧。
Is exhibit C the weapon that you say was used?
物證C是不是你說的所使用的武器？

NONE: B1 an event at which objects such as paintings are shown to the public, a situation in which someone shows a particular skill or quality to the public, or the act of showing these things
展覽（會）；表現，顯示

example: The photographs will be on exhibition until the end of the month.
這些照片將一直展出到月底。
There's a new exhibition of sculpture on at the city gallery.
市立美術館正在舉行一場新的雕塑作品展。
The athlete's third, and winning, jump was an exhibition of skill and strength.
這個運動員的第三次試跳，也是獲勝的那一跳，充分展示了他的技巧和體能。

NONE: › a single sports game that is not part of a larger competition, in which the players show their skills
表演賽
› disapproving behaviour that tries to attract attention
表演狂，表現癖；出風頭
› formal someone's enjoyment of showing their sexual organs in public
裸露癖；暴露狂

example: It's exhibitionism to flaunt wealth so blatantly.
如此招搖擺闊純粹是出風頭。

NONE: › someone who tries to attract attention to themselves by their behaviour
好出風頭者；好表現者
› psychology someone who shows their sexual organs in public
裸露癖患者；暴露狂

example: I have an exhibitionist streak that comes out on the dance floor.
我一到舞池上就會忍不住想要出出風頭。

NONE: › someone who has made or owns something, especially a work of art, shown in an exhibition
（尤指創作或擁有藝術品的）展出者，參展者

example: Many of the exhibitors will be at the gallery to meet the public.
很多參展者將在藝廊與大眾見面。

NONE: › to give someone strong feelings of happiness and excitement
使高興；使興奮；使激動萬分
› very excited and happy
異常興奮的；興高采烈的；心花怒放的

example: At the end of the race I was exhilarated.
比賽結束時我異常興奮。

NONE: › making you feel very excited and happy
令人極度興奮的；使人興高采烈的

example: an exhilarating walk in the mountains
令人興奮的山中漫步

NONE: › excitement and happiness
激動；興奮；高興
› to strongly encourage or try to persuade someone to do something
激勵；規勸；督促

example: The governor exhorted the prisoners not to riot.
獄長告誡犯人不要騷亂。

NONE: › to remove a dead body from the ground after it has been buried
（從墳墓中）掘出（屍體）
